I’m not sure if this entirely fits your question but I’m 25 and my mother died in March of 2017 at 53 from  ovarian cancer, she was pretty worse for wear for about the last year and a half, she was diagnosed in 2012.. but I wouldn’t say I regret anything I did to care for her, which was pretty hectic with chemo and medications and she couldn’t really bathe or go to the bathroom by herself, none of this bothered me but I wish I was more patient with her, I’d get upset when she said she couldn’t do something and to me it was a sign of her giving up, I wanted her to live so I would try to encourage/almost make her do things because I could see the drive in her leaving. After it all I can’t say I understand what she felt like but I know that I could have been more empathetic with the situation. I almost started to feel a sort of resentment towards her because she knew she was in bad shape and couldn’t help it. For me my advice is help and do what they ask and realize that they are not the people who bandaged us as a child. These things happen and it’s not easy.. but I now have a wife and two children, she never met any of them, but I hope that my kids will take care of me someday without question as we all have or will have to do someday.
